stories.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs lose $530 million in one day as broader market selloff rattles crypto
stories.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs saw a combined $530 million in net outflows in a single day. The exits came as a broader Wall Street selloff erased roughly $3 trillion in equity value. Crypto prices fell alongside stocks.
stories.whyItMatters: The outflows show how tightly crypto ETF demand now tracks broader risk sentiment, not just crypto-specific news.
whatToWatch: Whether outflows continue or reverse in coming sessions
Whether the stock selloff deepens or stabilizes
questions: What triggered the broader market wipeout?
Is this a short-term flow shift or a longer trend?

sources.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs lose $530 million in one day as $3 trillion Wall Street wipeout rattles crypto

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs bought nearly twice Q3 mined supply, then saw $430 million leave in a day
stories.summary: Bitcoin ETFs purchased close to double the bitcoin that miners produced in the third quarter, a sign of strong institutional demand. Flows reversed sharply on Thursday, with $430 million pulled out in one day.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF demand has been a key driver of bitcoin's supply-demand balance since the spot ETFs launched, so a sudden reversal matters for price support.
whatToWatch: Flow data in the days following Thursday's outflow
Whether Q4 demand still outpaces new mined supply
questions: Was Thursday's outflow a one-off or the start of a reversal?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs bought nearly twice what miners produced in Q3—but $430 million left on Thursday

stories.title: Bank of England raises rates to 4%, warns inflation could near 5% next year
stories.summary: The Bank of England raised its policy rate to 4%. The central bank forecast inflation could approach 5% next year, a sign it still sees price pressure ahead.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher rates and sticky inflation reduce appetite for risk assets, including crypto, and shape how traders read other central banks' next moves.
whatToWatch: The Bank of England's next policy meeting
Upcoming UK inflation data releases
questions: How will crypto markets price in a UK stagflation risk?

sources.title: Bank of England raises rates to 4% as it forecasts inflation near 5% next year

stories.title: NYSE-backed tokenization venture hit by 90% stock rejection and a liquidity shortfall
stories.summary: A crypto tokenization venture backed by the NYSE is reportedly facing a 90% rejection rate on stock listings, along with a liquidity problem put at $92. Details on the cause and scope remain thin.
stories.whyItMatters: A stumble at a major exchange-backed tokenization effort would test confidence in bringing traditional securities on-chain.
whatToWatch: Further detail on what the stock rejection figure covers
Whether the venture addresses the liquidity shortfall
questions: What exactly counts as a "rejected" stock in this case?

sources.title: NYSE-backed crypto venture faces 90% stock rejection as $92 liquidity problem threatens tokenization dream

stories.title: Binance cuts off SignalPlus after hackers used a fake Teams invite to break in
stories.summary: Binance severed its connection to trading platform SignalPlus after attackers compromised it. The hackers reportedly used a fake Microsoft Teams meeting invite to gain access.
stories.whyItMatters: The incident shows social-engineering attacks, not just code exploits, remain a top risk to crypto trading infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Whether user funds or data were affected
Binance's next steps on reconnecting or replacing the service
questions: How much access did the attackers gain before detection?

sources.title: Binance cuts off trading platform SignalPlus after hackers break in with a fake Teams invite

stories.title: Researchers say cheap online services routed traffic through a White House-linked network
stories.summary: Researchers reported that low-cost online services routed web traffic through a network linked to the White House. Few other details on the services or the network have been disclosed.
stories.whyItMatters: Questions about who controls internet infrastructure used by online services matter for anyone relying on it for secure, private access.
whatToWatch: Further detail from researchers on the affected services
Any official response to the findings
questions: Which services and network are involved?
Was the routing intentional or a misconfiguration?

sources.title: Cheap online services routed web traffic through a White House-linked network, researchers say

stories.title: Bitcoin's rate-cut relief stalls as service-sector inflation flares back up
stories.summary: Bitcoin's earlier rally on hopes for interest rate cuts has stalled. New data show service-sector inflation picking up, which complicates the case for near-term cuts.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's price has moved closely with rate-cut expectations, so renewed inflation pressure could delay the easing traders were counting on.
whatToWatch: Upcoming inflation reports
Signals from the Fed on its next policy move
questions: Will the Fed still cut rates despite the inflation data?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s rate cut relief stalls as service inflation flares

stories.title: FBI agent accused of draining crypto wallets from 35 cases, stealing $2.47 million
stories.summary: An FBI agent allegedly drained crypto wallets connected to 35 separate investigations, taking about $2.47 million. The agent reportedly planned to flee to Portugal.
stories.whyItMatters: The case raises concerns about how law enforcement secures seized crypto assets and whether evidence in dozens of cases was compromised.
whatToWatch: Formal charges and prosecution of the agent
Any policy changes to how agencies custody seized crypto
questions: What happens to the 35 affected investigations?

sources.title: FBI agent drains crypto wallets tied to 35 investigations, steals $2.47 million and plans Portugal escape

stories.title: Unpatched Bitcoin Lightning nodes exposed to channel-draining bug
stories.summary: A bug in the Bitcoin Lightning Network can drain payment channels on nodes that have not applied a fix. Node operators who have not patched remain at risk.
stories.whyItMatters: Lightning underpins bitcoin's fast-payment layer, so an unpatched flaw threatens funds held in open channels.
whatToWatch: How quickly node operators apply the patch
Reports of the bug being exploited in the wild
questions: Has any operator already lost funds to this bug?

sources.title: Unpatched Bitcoin Lightning nodes face channel-draining bug

stories.title: XRP sellers hit with heavy slippage as USD order book depth proves misleading
stories.summary: XRP sellers reportedly faced large slippage after the depth shown in USD order books turned out to overstate real available size. The report points to a gap between displayed and actual liquidity.
stories.whyItMatters: If order book depth cannot be trusted, traders may misjudge execution risk and true market liquidity for XRP.
whatToWatch: Whether exchanges address the order book discrepancy
Follow-up analysis on which venues were affected
questions: Which exchange or exchanges were examined?
Is this isolated to XRP or a wider market issue?

sources.title: XRP sellers face massive slip as USD order book depth fakes size
